intended_object: The augmentation chain map ε : P → k[0]. Here P is the 2-periodic complex ⋯ → k[G] →N k[G] →(g−1) k[G] → 0 for a finite cyclic group G = ⟨g⟩, and k[0] is the trivial representation k placed in degree 0. In degree 0, ε sends x ∈ k[G] to the sum of its coefficients. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `resolution_quasiIso` / `resolution`.
explanation:
A chain map from P to a complex concentrated in degree 0 is the same thing as one morphism d : P₀ → k with d ∘ (P₁ → P₀) = 0. The definition uses exactly this description, through `toSingle₀Equiv`.

The degree-0 component is `leftRegularHom (trivial k G k) 1`. This is the G-equivariant map k[G] → k determined by 1 ↦ 1. It sends `single h r` to r·ρ(h)(1) = r, so it is the sum of coefficients, i.e. the usual augmentation map. The proof obligation, augmentation ∘ (ρ(g) − 1) = 0, holds trivially.

The setting is appropriate:
- `CommGroup G` is needed so that ρ(g) − 1 is a morphism of representations, and finite cyclic groups are abelian anyway.
- `Fintype G` is needed for the norm map.
- The definition does not assume that g generates G, because the chain map exists for any g. The hypothesis only enters when proving the quasi-isomorphism.

This is the standard augmentation of the periodic resolution for cyclic groups. Mathlib has no more general version of this particular chain map; the augmentation of the bar resolution is a different object.
